name: Kokoda
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Read de Vries 2004 (PL 560) Kokoda appendix pp.130-137 via ANU repository: phone inventory and wordlist only, no stress statement; Berry & Berry 1987 survey not online.

new_statements.citation: one of the works listed for this language (see the second reader's note)
new_statements.check: reported by the second reader, not yet confirmed
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work is listed for koko1265 and it was opened and read; no silent or unopened works remain to spot-check. Re-reading every page of that work that mentions Kokoda (pp. 570, 581, 582, 586, 593, 594, 622) turned up no stress statement beyond what the reader reported; the only unreported Kokoda datum is the accented form notúa-ra-ba in example (25), p. 593 (PDF p. 26), quoted from de Vries 2004: 135, which marks stress on one word but states no rule and is not a statement about Kokoda stress.

sources.note: Consonant/vowel tables copied from de Vries 2004; no stress or accent information. Lists dialects Negeri Besar, Kasuweri (Komudago), Tarof, Yamueti and ethnonym Emeyode (from Ethnologue).

sources.citation: Holton, Gary & Marian Klamer. 2018. The Papuan languages of East Nusantara and the Bird's Head. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area, 569-640. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Areal survey with a phonology/prosody section per family; may summarise SBH stress second-hand (probably from de Vries 2004 Inanwatan) — would only give a family-level statement.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens J. 2004. "The Kokoda language" (Appendix 3 §1, pp. 129-137). In: A short grammar of Inanwatan, an endangered language of the Bird's Head of Papua, Indonesia. Pacific Linguistics 560. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-560
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement for Kokoda. §1.1 'Kokoda phone inventory' (p.130) gives consonant/vowel charts and 'There are no CC clusters no word-final C in the data.'; §1.2 (pp.131-133) is a 209-item wordlist in which stress is marked with IPA ' and falls on different syllables in different items ('kokoda 'lake', wa'kawa 'head', kaka'pirumo 'dirty', o'bora 'hand'), but no rule is drawn. Only 4 hours of survey elicitation (Kasueri dialect informants, 18 Sept 1995).

sources.note: Nothing for Kokoda. §2.6.2.3.4.1 'The South Bird's Head Family' pp.438-440: 'There is almost no grammatical information on all these languages'; the single phonological remark ('a striking feature of the sound system is a strong bilabial fricative; the accent is a high-pitch accent', p.438) refers to Barau (= Kemberano, bzp), not Tarof/Kasuweri.
